# Dock layouts have no maximize — a first-class pane maximize for tabs nodes

## The gap

Qt-parity dock UIs ship a maximize affordance on every dock pane; `src/dashboard/dock` has none — `grep -rn maximize src/dashboard/` yields one hit, and it is the assignment-math wording in `TopologyReconciler`, not a feature. Consumers can hand-roll an overlay through the host header-action seam, but each one re-derives the same design decisions (state, restore, animation, keyboard). The dock should own it, the way it owns `close` behind `enableDockCloseAction`.

## Design sketch (the pieces already exist)

- **Affordance:** an engine-owned header action behind `enableDockMaximizeAction`, rendered by `projection.LayoutAdapter` next to `close` and *owned* by `dashboard.dock.Workspace#onDockHeaderAction` rather than re-emitted (the `close` precedent, including the reserved-name guard the adapter already throws for). Icon pair + toggle semantics as in `dialog.Base` (`maximizeCls`/`minimizeCls`).
- **Mechanism — presentation, not topology:** maximize the **tabs node in place** via a class toggle (`neo-dock-maximized`) plus a MEASURED rect: `position: fixed` with `top/left/width/height` set to the workspace root's viewport rect at toggle time — never `inset: 0`, which answers to the viewport or an incidental fixed containing block instead of the workspace. The class carries everything static (z-index, transitions); the four rect values are per-instance inline style. The header stays visible carrying the restore button.
- **Hard constraint — no DOM re-parenting:** a maximized pane must keep DOM identity. Panes hosting an iframe reload their browsing context on re-parent (losing embedded-app state); canvas and video lose state the same way. This rules out floating-container/DOM-move implementations and rules out expressing maximize as a committed topology mutation the reconciler could satisfy by rebuilding nodes.
- **State:** a workspace-local transient (public `maximizedNodeId`, defined as `maximizedNodeId_` in static config), deliberately **not** part of the committed dock document — maximize is presentation. Perspectives, persistence, and topology diffs never see it. **Re-projection is deterministic:** after any re-projection, the workspace re-applies the maximize presentation iff `maximizedNodeId_` still resolves to a projected tabs node, and clears the transient otherwise (the node was closed/merged away) — never a third outcome, never baked into the model.
- **Motion:** FLIP from the node's pre-maximize rect (the `DockFlip` addon already animates dock re-layouts; a first/last transform against one node is its trivial case). Instant-path fallbacks per DockFlip's own contract (`prefers-reduced-motion`, hidden documents).
- **Input contract (frozen, see ledger):** in-strip tab reordering stays live while maximized (it never leaves the node); cross-zone drag sources and tear-out affordances for the maximized node are suppressed while maximized — every drop target is under the overlay, so offering the gesture would be fixture-dishonest. `Escape` restores, owned by the workspace's `KeyboardCommands` scope and active only while `maximizedNodeId` is set; after restore, focus returns to the restored tabs node's active header button. The maximized plane z-orders above rails and the reveal overlay; engaging maximize closes an in-progress reveal (one overlay at a time). Any committed dock operation that reaches beyond the maximized node clears maximize BEFORE applying, and that clear is terminal — the re-projection rule re-applies only a transient that survived, never one an operation cleared. Operations confined to the maximized node (activating one of its tabs; closing, reordering or adding an item within it) do not pre-clear: they defer to the same deterministic rule, which re-applies onto the surviving node and clears when the node collapsed away — without this confinement, switching tabs inside a maximized pane would restore it on the second click of any real session. Double-click on the tab header stays an optional second affordance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `enableDockMaximizeAction` renders an engine-owned toggle action on tabs-node headers; the reserved-name guard covers it like `close`.
- [ ] Maximize/restore never re-parents the pane's DOM: a headless spec pins element identity (the same node before, during, and after) and asserts an iframe child is not reloaded.
- [ ] Maximized state is workspace-transient: the committed document and a saved/restored perspective are byte-identical whether or not a pane was maximized when captured.
- [ ] The maximized node paints the full workspace rect (headless rect assertion) and `Escape` restores.
- [ ] Operations confined to the maximized node (tab activation, in-node close) keep it maximized; any operation beyond it clears before applying — both spec-witnessed.
- [ ] FLIP motion on both transitions with DockFlip's instant-path degradations intact.

## Contract Ledger (consumed cells)

| Cell | Producer | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| header action surface | `projection.LayoutAdapter` renders engine-owned actions next to host actions; ownership dispatch in `dashboard.dock.Workspace#onDockHeaderAction` (the `close` precedent, reserved-name guard included) | `enableDockMaximizeAction: false` (default) renders nothing — byte-identical projection for every current consumer; `true` renders the toggle on tabs-node headers | Off by default | The option name + the reserved-name guard error text | `close`/`enableDockCloseAction` shipping today; the guard already throws on host-action collisions |
| maximized presentation + geometry | `dashboard.dock.Workspace` stamps `neo-dock-maximized` on the target tabs node's projected root AND supplies the rect: it measures its own root el's viewport rect (`DomAccess.getBoundingClientRect` on the workspace id — the workspace is the authority, no containing-block assumption) and sets `top/left/width/height` inline | The node paints the measured workspace rect; header stays visible carrying the restore toggle; NO DOM re-parenting (spec pins element identity + iframe-not-reloaded). **Resize while maximized:** a NEW Workspace-owned observation — no existing one covers this: on maximize, the Workspace registers its root el with the `ResizeObserver` main-thread addon (the `grid.Container#addResizeObserver` idiom: `getAddon('ResizeObserver', windowId)` + `register({id})`); the handler re-measures and re-applies the four values; restore, node-clear, and workspace destroy all unregister — the observation exists exactly as long as the presentation does, no standing cost while un-maximized. **Fail-safe:** an unresolvable measurement (workspace unmounted mid-gesture, zero-area rect) clears `maximizedNodeId` and removes the class — the restore path, never a half state | Cleared state = normal layout | SCSS block comment naming the no-reparent + measured-rect constraints | `dialog.Base#afterSetMaximized` for the cls-toggle half; `DockFlip`'s rect measurement for the measure-then-style idiom |

| transient state × re-projection | `maximizedNodeId_` on the workspace instance — never written into the committed document | Deterministic re-projection rule above: re-apply iff the node id resolves in the new projection, clear otherwise. Perspectives capture/restore byte-identical documents regardless of maximize state (AC) | Cleared state = normal layout | The config's jsdoc carries the rule | AC pins document + perspective byte-equality and both re-projection outcomes |
| motion | `main.addon.DockFlip` FLIP from the pre-toggle rect | Instant-path degradations per DockFlip's own contract (`prefers-reduced-motion`, hidden documents, frame-starved windows) | Instant land | DockFlip class jsdoc (already written) | DockFlip ships with these paths spec-covered |

Requested as proper engine support after a consumer-workspace exploration (agent session 914dffcd-0057-46a5-a0c6-9ca807fd5c91) concluded a client-side overlay would re-derive dock-owned decisions. Existing primitives are real: `dialog.Base` owns class-toggle maximize/icon semantics; `LayoutAdapter` + `Workspace#onDockHeaderAction` own stable engine/host actions; `DockFlip` owns fail-safe motion; `KeyboardCommands` owns discrete dock commands.
- **Historical amnesia / debt radar:** targeted Memory Core searches for dock maximize, DOM-identity preservation, and Dialog/DockFlip reuse found no prior maximize decision. Relevant prior sessions reinforce the living canon: `DockWorkspace` owns projection composition and presentation state must not become topology.

### Retrospective six-stage verdict

Premise, substrate, consumer, and service boundaries pass: maximize is a genuine missing dock capability, belongs in the Dock workspace/projection layer, and must preserve worker-owned topology plus DOM identity. No parallel layout or drag system is proposed.

### Readiness blocker

The ticket introduces/changes consumed surfaces but has no Contract Ledger:

| Required row | Contract that must be frozen |
|---|---|
| `enableDockMaximizeAction` + reserved `maximize` action | producer, projected action order/icon/toggle behavior, disabled/hidden conditions, host-name collision, fallback when off |
| `maximizedNodeId` transient state | owner, initial/null semantics, node removal, workspace destroy, re-projection, perspective capture/restore exclusion, multi-window scope |
| DOM/CSS presentation mechanism | exact node/class owner, workspace-rect authority, stacking/focus, no-reparent guarantee, iframe/canvas/video identity witness, containing-block fallback |
| Maximize/restore motion | DockFlip call sequence, instant paths (reduced motion/hidden document/failure), truth never waiting on animation |
| Input/interplay | Escape ownership and focus return; tab/header drag policy while maximized; rails/reveal overlay ordering; restore behavior before any operation that cannot run maximized |

One phrase must become deterministic before code:

> “a re-projection while maximized re-applies the class **or drops the state**”

Choose one contract. Recommended invariant: if the same tabs node survives, reapply maximize to the reconciled node; if the node no longer exists, clear the transient state and restore ordinary presentation. Never silently “drop” state while leaving presentation ambiguous.

**Classification:** `needs-contract-alignment`. Positive ROI, correct substrate, no duplicate; assignment/branch/code remain off until the ledger lands and intake rechecks it.

### @neo-gpt - 2026-08-31T11:12:08Z

## `[TICKET_INTAKE][STILL_BLOCKED]` — deterministic re-projection passes; geometry and input contracts do not

The new `transient state × re-projection` row closes the ambiguity I named: surviving tabs node ⇒ reapply; missing node ⇒ clear; committed documents/perspectives remain untouched.

Two readiness gates still fail:

### 1. The selected CSS mechanism has no workspace-rect authority

The body promises “full workspace rect” but selects `position: fixed; inset: 0`. A fixed box is viewport-relative unless an ancestor establishes a fixed containing block; that ancestor is then the authority, not the dock workspace. Current `dashboard.dock.Workspace` declares the `neo-dock-workspace` anchor but no engine contract makes it the fixed containing block. For a nested dock workspace, the selected rule can therefore cover the viewport or an incidental transformed ancestor rather than the workspace.

Please update the presentation row to name:

- the source of the target workspace rect / containing block;
- behavior under workspace resize while maximized;
- the fail-safe when that geometry cannot be resolved.

The no-reparent constraint remains sound; the missing piece is how the same node is made workspace-relative.

### 2. The required input/interplay cell is absent

The design sketch still contains unresolved alternatives (“suppress cross-zone drag sources **or** restore-on-dragstart”) and the ledger has no input row. Freeze one contract for:

- drag start while maximized;
- `Escape` ownership plus focus return;
- rails/reveal-overlay ordering;
- restore before an operation that cannot remain maximized.

Also name the instance surface as public `maximizedNodeId` (defined by `maximizedNodeId_` in static config), so the ledger does not imply an instance property ending in `_`.

**Classification remains:** `needs-contract-alignment`. The feature and substrate are valid; assignment/branch/code stay off until these consumed behaviors are deterministic.

### @neo-gpt - 2026-08-31T11:32:18Z

## `[TICKET_INTAKE][STILL_BLOCKED]` — geometry/input contracts pass; resize producer does not exist

The measured-rect mechanism, fail-safe clear, frozen input row, public `maximizedNodeId` surface, and deterministic re-projection rule now close the two gates from the prior intake.

One Surface-Anchor V-B-A still fails:

> “the workspace’s existing resize observation re-measures and re-applies the four values”

At Engine `dev@32eebf7733b2`, `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` has no ResizeObserver registration or resize handler. The generic `container.Base` does not supply one either; the existing engine precedents are opt-in owners such as `container.Viewport`, `component.Canvas`, `component.Helix`, and `component.MagicMoveText`. So the ledger currently names a producer that is absent.

Please make the selected contract exact:

- name a **new Workspace-owned** ResizeObserver registration/unregistration + handler as part of this ticket, including destroy/unmount cleanup, **or**
- remove live remeasurement from the promise and state the bounded resize behavior honestly.

Because AC-4 requires the maximized node to paint the full workspace rect, the first option is the coherent fit. No other ledger row needs reopening.

**Classification remains:** `needs-contract-alignment` on this one producer only. No assignment or branch.
